page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and built on the x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing a dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves average tier performance in single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core evaluations. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also perform in the average range. However, multi-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores falling into the bottom 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is similarly limited, with both cached and uncached read/write operations registering in the lower percentiles.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfg7.large offers dedicated CPU resources at a low-density entry point, making it suitable for workloads where CPU sharing is undesirable but overall resource demands are modest. Due to the poor multi-core scaling, low memory bandwidth, and lack of local storage, it is not suited for database operations, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or high-throughput web serving. Appropriate workloads are limited to light single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-traffic general-purpose tasks.
